  5. Show HN: Mastra Factory, the open-source software factory we use to build Mastra

    • AI
    • Open Source
    • Software Development

    145 points · 42 comments · 18 Nov 2026, 16:53 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Mastra Factory is an open-source, configurable agentic kanban system for software work, operated through a web UI and Slack. Its self-post says Mastra uses durable agents, memory, a cited Markdown wiki, PR-comment signals, cloud sandboxes, and a coding harness; it reports 238 Factory-opened-and-merged PRs and 630 human PRs in one week, alongside hosted and self-hosted options.

    Discussion — Discussion centered on the maintainers' decision to close their main repository to outside contributors because of low-value automated PRs, while requesting high-quality issue reproductions. Readers asked how autonomy, plans, model/harness integration, agent identity, UX validation, and human approval work. The team said lower-risk work can be more automated and that sandbox preview environments support UI testing.

  7. Google's AI answers reducing search traffic by 40%

    • AI
    • Economics
    • Search Engines

    709 points · 563 comments · 18 Nov 2026, 00:17 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — RevScope argues that Google AI Overviews reduce outbound clicks, citing a randomized desktop-Chrome experiment in which visible Overviews averaged fewer external clicks and estimating an overall organic-click loss. The article combines that working paper with observational Pew and DataForSEO material, states limitations in the modeling and sampling, and finds little demonstrated value in GEO tactics beyond conventional SEO and reputable third-party presence.

    Discussion — The thread debated whether AI answers undermine publishers, hobby communities, and other sources that fund public information, or mainly displace low-value SEO and ad-heavy content. Commenters also discussed copyright, citations, paywalls, revenue sharing, Google’s earlier incentives, and whether search should prioritize direct primary sources; the author acknowledged possible commercial-query bias in one dataset.

  10. Show HN: Open-source, real-time object tracking for live video feeds

    • AI

    120 points · 13 comments · 16 Nov 2026, 21:14 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — tamserve is an Apache-2.0 Python serving engine for real-time, multi-camera object tracking using SAM 2, EdgeTAM, and optionally SAM 3 for text prompts. It shares model instances across cameras and dynamically batches work; its README reports lower GPU-memory use and higher aggregate throughput than the model's stock per-camera code in specified EdgeTAM/RTX 4090 benchmarks, while reporting essentially unchanged DAVIS 2017 accuracy.

    Discussion — The short thread congratulated the release, pointed to a separate browser-based live-video project, and included a vendor comment promoting a SAM 3.1 low-latency API. One commenter asked that the large GIF be replaced with video; another asked about reposting etiquette because the project had appeared on HN days earlier.

    • Economics

  14. All AI-generated code should be Open Source

    • AI
    • Copyright
    • Open Source

    1285 points · 673 comments · 15 Nov 2026, 14:46 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — The essay argues that AI-generated code should be open source, citing training on publicly available material and uncertainty around copyrightability of purely AI-generated output. It distinguishes fully automated output from mixed human-and-AI authorship but favors open release for lightly reviewed or prompt-only code.

    Discussion — The dominant response was that public-domain status is not the same as open source: copyright is generally needed to impose open-source license conditions. Commenters also disputed whether AI-assisted code is necessarily uncopyrightable and whether the proposed rule is workable.

    Week of 2026-11-20

  15. Show HN: DeepSeek V3 in ~200 lines of pure Jax

    • AI
    • Education

    276 points · 30 comments · 14 Nov 2026, 15:04 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — A MIT-licensed, educational JAX reimplementation of selected DeepSeek-V3 ideas in about 190 lines: multi-head latent attention, DeepSeekMoE, bias-based expert balancing, and multi-token prediction. The repository documents a 36.2M-parameter run trained on 207 public-domain detective books on a 24GB MacBook Air M5, and publishes its checkpoint, data, tests, and reproduction instructions.

    Discussion — Readers praised the readable first-principles implementation and asked for a clearer inventory of what is omitted versus DeepSeek-V3.
